newsitem.title: USA: S. Dakota wheat 91 percent harvested vs 82 average.
newsitem.headline: S. Dakota wheat 91 percent harvested vs 82 average.

text.p: South Dakota's spring wheat harvest was wrapping up in the week ended Sunday but dry weather hurt row crops and pasture, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly report.
Spring wheat was 91 percent harvested, compared with the five-year average of 82 percent.
But continued dry weather caused corn and soybean ratings to decline. The acreage rated good to excellent dropped 13 and 11 points, respectively.
Corn borers and grasshoppers were reported in the southern half of the state.
Corn progress was behind average with 44 percent in the dough stage versus 55 percent average.
Soybeans were 93 percent setting pods, ahead of average of 84 percent.
Pasture was rated two percent very poor, seven percent poor, 31 percent fair, 55 percent good and five percent excellent.
Soil moisture was rated 15 percent very short, 41 percent short, 43 percent adequate and one percent surplus.
